newsitem.title: MEXICO: Mexico peso closes soft as foreigners leave bourse.
newsitem.headline: Mexico peso closes soft as foreigners leave bourse.

text.p: The Mexican peso closed weaker across the board on Thursday after foreign investors took profits and stepped out of the bourse and after local dealers covered dollar positions, traders said.
"The market closed with the dollar in demand, under pressure from foreigners taking profits on the bourse and locals who had gone short covering positions," a trader said.
The benchmark 48-hour peso and its 24-hour stablemate closed 2.8 and two centavos weaker, respectively, at 7.8310/7.8360 and 7.8190/7.8240 per dollar.
Same-day peso contracts earlier closed 0.8 of a centavo weaker at 7.8070/7.8120 per dollar.
The leading IPC index of Mexican shares was down 0.85 percent at 3,696.32 points when the foreign exchange market closed.
"The New Year rally seems to be over, the market was very active and nervous," another trader said.
Other traders put the peso's weakness down to increased yields on U.S. 30-year Treasury bonds, up to 6.85 percent, from 6.75 percent in late trade on Wednesday.
